name: Code/Loop-Based Time Complexity Derivation
recognitionClueHinglish: C code/pseudocode diya hai (loops ke saath, shayad nested, shayad loop-bound variable-dependent) aur poocha hai time complexity ya total number of operations kya hai — ye is topic ka sabse bada pattern hai (31 me se 7 PYQs).
whatShouldComeToMind: Write the iteration count as an explicit summation first — don't guess.
Triangular nested loops (inner bound = outer index) are STILL Θ(n²), just half the constant.
Loop variable multiplied/divided each iteration (not +1/-1) signals Θ(log n).
generalSolvingApproach: 1. For each loop, express its iteration count as a function of the relevant variable(s).
2. For nested loops, write the TOTAL as a nested summation (Σ_i Σ_j ...).
3. Evaluate the summation using standard formulas.
4. Simplify to the dominant term for the final Θ/O answer.
variationsObserved: Loop bound tied to an array's contents (a[i]==1 conditionally calling a sub-function) — need to reason about worst-case total work across the whole loop, not per-iteration in isolation.
Triple-nested loop with dependent bounds (i, j=i to n, k=j+1 to n) — combinatorial counting (number of increasing triples).
commonTraps: Treating a triangular nested loop as a different complexity CLASS instead of recognizing it's still Θ(n²).
Missing a hidden logarithmic loop disguised as a while-loop with multiplicative update.

name: Minimum/Optimal Comparison-Count (Lower Bound) Problems
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai 'minimum number of comparisons needed' ya 'tightest lower/upper bound' for a specific classic task (find max, find max+min, find duplicate, check sorted) — is topic ka doosra bada pattern (31 me se 10 PYQs), calculation nahi, classical-result-recall + reasoning hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Recognize which CLASSICAL problem this is (max-finding = n-1, max+min together = ⌈3n/2⌉-2, comparison-sort lower bound = Ω(n log n)).
For less-classical problems, apply information-theoretic reasoning: ⌈log_k(number of possible outcomes)⌉.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Identify the exact task (single extremum? both extrema? checking a property? finding a specific element?).
2. If it matches a known classical result, recall the tight bound directly.
3. If novel, count the number of possible distinct outcomes N, and the number of outcomes distinguishable per comparison k, apply ⌈log_k N⌉.
4. Distinguish 'worst-case minimum guaranteed' (a proven lower bound) from just 'an algorithm that achieves X comparisons' (an upper bound, which may not be tight).
variationsObserved: Comparing TWO different algorithms'/packages' complexity to find a crossover point (find smallest n where one becomes better than the other — solve an inequality).
Finding an element that's 'neither max nor min' — needs a specific counting argument, not a standard formula.
commonTraps: Confusing an achievable UPPER bound (some algorithm's comparison count) with the PROVEN tight LOWER bound (the true minimum possible) — GATE questions are precise about which one they're asking.

name: Recursive Function Time Complexity (via recurrence)
recognitionClueHinglish: Recursive C function/algorithm diya hai aur poocha hai iski time complexity kya hai — ye Recurrence Relation topic ka direct crossover hai; yahan focus 'set up recurrence then classify complexity' pe hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Set up T(n) from the recursive calls + non-recursive work (same as Recurrence Relation Pattern 02).
Solve using Master Theorem or recursion tree (Recurrence Relation Pattern 01) to get the final Θ/O class.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Identify recursive calls and their reduced arguments.
3. Set up and solve the recurrence (reuse Recurrence Relation techniques).
4. Compare against an ITERATIVE version of the same problem if the question asks for a comparison (recursive vs iterative complexity).
variationsObserved: Side-by-side comparison of a naive-recursive (exponential) vs dynamic-programming/iterative (polynomial) version of the SAME problem — classic 'recognize the DP speedup' question.
commonTraps: Not recognizing that a recursive function calling itself MULTIPLE times per invocation (like naive Fibonacci-style f1 calling itself twice) gives EXPONENTIAL complexity, contrasted sharply with an iterative/memoized O(n) version.

name: Mathematical/Numeric Algorithm Complexity (exponentiation, root-finding, matrix layout)
recognitionClueHinglish: Ek numeric/mathematical algorithm hai (jaise x^n compute karna, cube root nikaalna, matrix multiply with row/column-major layout) aur poocha hai iski complexity — ye domain-specific numeric-algorithm pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Exponentiation by squaring: computing x^n needs only O(log n) multiplications (not O(n)) by repeatedly squaring and combining based on binary representation of n.

Matrix multiplication complexity is affected by memory LAYOUT (row-major vs column-major) due to cache locality, not just the raw operation count — connects to the Cache Memory topic's loop-locality pattern.
conceptsRequired: Cache-locality effects on matrix algorithms (cross-link to CO&A)
generalSolvingApproach: 1. For exponentiation-style problems, think in terms of the BINARY representation of the exponent — each bit either requires a multiply-and-square or just a square.
2. For matrix/array-layout problems, reason about which traversal order matches the storage layout (reuse the Loop/Locality pattern from Cache Memory topic).
variationsObserved: Binary-search-style numeric root-finding (cube root via binary search over candidate values).
commonTraps: Assuming naive O(n) multiplication is needed for x^n instead of recognizing the O(log n) squaring trick.

name: Misc/Advanced (game trees, geometric algorithms, matching-type)
recognitionClueHinglish: Specialized/advanced algorithmic scenario (game-tree minimax, computational geometry steepest-line problem, match-the-pairs) — low-frequency, read carefully and apply general algorithmic reasoning rather than a memorized formula.
whatShouldComeToMind: No single formula — identify the underlying algorithmic technique (search, sort, divide-and-conquer) the scenario is really testing.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Strip away the domain-specific framing (game/geometry) to find the underlying computational problem.
2. Apply the relevant general technique (search tree analysis, sorting-based approach, etc.).
